blocks.content: The metadata block holds an object's identity, name, namespace, labels, and annotations, alongside a handful of fields the system manages entirely on its own.
The fields you typically write yourself are name, namespace, labels, and annotations, together forming an object's identity and organizational metadata.

blocks.alt: The identity and organizational fields you actually author yourself

blocks.content:
metadata:
  name: my-app
  namespace: production
  labels:
    app: my-app
  annotations:
    description: "Handles user requests"

blocks.content: 2. name Must Be Unique Within Its Scope
blocks.text: 2. name Must Be Unique Within Its Scope

blocks.content: An object's name must be unique within its scope, within a namespace for namespaced resources, or cluster-wide for cluster-scoped ones (like the PersistentVolumes covered in the Storage module).

blocks.alt: Unique within the relevant scope, namespace-wide or cluster-wide, depending on the resource type

blocks.content: Both fields are covered in full depth in their own dedicated topics in the Pods module, labels for selection and grouping, annotations for non-selectable metadata, this topic is simply where they live structurally.

blocks.alt: Full depth already covered in the Pods module, this is where they structurally live

blocks.content: Beyond what you write, metadata also holds fields the system manages entirely on its own: uid (a globally unique identifier), resourceVersion (covered in the Internals module's etcd Data Storage topic), and creationTimestamp, none of these are ever something you set yourself.

blocks.alt: Fields the system populates and manages, never something you write yourself

blocks.content: Put together, metadata is really two categories of fields living in one block, what you deliberately author, and what the system tracks automatically alongside it.

blocks.alt: Two genuinely different categories of fields, coexisting in the same block

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: metadata holds the fields you author (name, namespace, labels, annotations) alongside system-managed fields (uid, resourceVersion, creationTimestamp) you never set yourself.
name must be unique within its relevant scope, namespace-wide for most resources, cluster-wide for the cluster-scoped exceptions covered in the Storage module.
